definitionEn: to create a strong relationship, agreement or connection through hard work
senseNote: Здесь — «налаживать, выстраивать» (forge ties, forge an alliance); значение «подделывать» (forge a signature) не тренируем.
situation: Two people, companies or countries work hard to build a lasting partnership, friendship or agreement.

examples.text: The two rival airlines [[forged]] a partnership that now lets passengers book both companies' flights on one ticket.
The new principal wants to [[forge]] closer links between the college and local employers.
At university she [[forged]] friendships that are still going strong thirty years later.

texts: Small firms often struggle to [[forge]] ties with big retailers.
A difficult shared project can [[forge]] real team spirit.
The treaty helped the two former enemies [[forge]] a lasting peace.

badCollocation.noteRu: С документами forge значит «подделать»: forge a contract — подделать договор. Заключить договор — sign a contract; forge — про союзы и связи.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ an alliance with a rival company
collocationTask.explanationRu: Forge an alliance — заключить союз, выстроить партнёрство. Do, take и draw с alliance не сочетаются: говорят form, build или forge an alliance.

nuance.text: Over ten years, the museum has [[forged]] close ties with schools across the region.
nuance.explanationRu: Forge ties — выстроить прочные связи ценой усилий. Make с ties и partnership звучит неестественно: make обычно в make friends, make contacts.

reverse.text: She found it easy to [[make]] friends at her new school.
reverse.explanationRu: Заводить друзей — make friends. Forge сочетается не с людьми, а с отношениями: forge a friendship, forge ties.

fixIt.text: The new ambassador hopes to [[adjust]] closer ties between our two countries.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Наладить связи» — не adjust (подстроить, отрегулировать), а forge ties: создать прочные отношения.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "How did the trade fair in Berlin go?"
options: Really well. We forged some useful links with two German suppliers.
Really well. We forged a lovely lunch at a German restaurant.
Affirmative. Strategic linkages were forged with supply-side stakeholders.
reply.explanationRu: Forge links — наладить полезные связи. Обед словом forge не описывают. Третий ответ звучит как канцелярский отчёт, а не разговор с коллегой.

rewrite.original: The two companies built their partnership during the financial crisis.
rewrite.frame: The partnership between the two companies ____ during the financial crisis.
rewrite.explanationRu: Нужен пассив: the partnership was forged — союз был выстроен.

definitionEn: a method or set of principles that reliably produces a particular result
senseNote: Здесь — «рецепт, способ добиться результата» (a formula for success); математическая или химическая формула — базовое значение.
situation: Talking about a proven method or combination of things that usually leads to success or a particular result.

examples.text: The show's [[formula]] never changes: three amateur cooks, one mystery ingredient and a strict time limit.
There's no magic [[formula]] for building a successful start-up; it takes luck and years of hard work.
After weeks of talks, the parties agreed on a [[formula]] for sharing power in the new coalition.

texts: Good food and friendly staff: that's the [[formula]] behind their success.
Many romantic comedies follow the same predictable [[formula]].
There is no simple [[formula]] for raising happy children.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Формула успеха» — a formula for success, с предлогом for. The formula of — о химической или математической формуле: the formula of water.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Формула успеха — a formula (или a recipe) for success. Receipt — чек, а не рецепт; form — бланк или форма, formation — образование или строй.

nuance.text: Negotiators finally found a [[formula]] that allowed both sides to claim victory.
nuance.explanationRu: Formula — выработанная схема, способ решить задачу; так говорят и о переговорах. Recipe — прежде всего кулинарный рецепт, а в переносном смысле чаще a recipe for disaster.

reverse.text: Could you send me your [[recipe]] for that lemon cake?
reverse.explanationRu: Кулинарный рецепт — recipe. Formula рядом с тортом прозвучит как химическая формула или детская смесь.

fixIt.text: There's no secret [[receipt]] for a happy marriage; you just keep talking to each other.
fixIt.explanationRu: Receipt — чек из магазина, а не «рецепт». Способ добиться результата — formula: a formula for a happy marriage.

wordFormation.text: Critics called the film [[formulaic]]: the plot followed every rule of the genre.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Your team hit every target this year. How did you do it?"
options: Honestly, the formula was very kind to us and gave us extra time.
The formula underpinning our performance shall be disclosed in due course.
Honestly, there's no magic formula. We just planned carefully and talked a lot.
reply.explanationRu: No magic formula — «нет волшебного рецепта». Formula не может быть «добра» к людям, это не человек. Второй ответ звучит как пресс-релиз, а не разговор с коллегой.

definitionEn: to develop a plan, policy or idea carefully, working out all the details
situation: A team or government carefully develops a detailed plan, policy or strategy before acting.

examples.text: The ministry has six months to [[formulate]] a new policy on air pollution in cities.
Before collecting any data, researchers should [[formulate]] a clear hypothesis.
Our team spent the whole afternoon [[formulating]] a response to the client's complaint.

texts: Parents and teachers met to [[formulate]] new rules on mobile phones.
It took the scientist years to [[formulate]] her theory of memory.
The new manager must [[formulate]] a clear strategy for growth.

badCollocation.noteRu: Решение не formulate, а make или reach: make a decision. Formulate — разрабатывать план, политику, теорию.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Разработать стратегию — formulate a strategy. Compose — сочинять музыку или письмо, perform — исполнять, pronounce — произносить.

nuance.text: The committee spent months [[formulating]] detailed guidelines for online teaching.
nuance.explanationRu: Formulate — продумать и разработать план, правила, теорию. Form — создать, образовать: form a committee, form a group. Продуманную разработку правил form не передаёт.

reverse.text: The students [[formed]] a committee to organise the graduation party.
reverse.explanationRu: Создать комитет или группу — form. Formulate относится к идеям и планам, а не к организациям.

fixIt.text: Our department has [[composed]] a new policy on working from home.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Составить политику, план» — не compose (сочинять музыку, текст), а formulate или draw up.

wordFormation.text: The [[formulation]] of the new safety rules took almost a year.

rewrite.original: The committee needs to develop a clear plan for the new library.
rewrite.frame: A clear plan for the new library needs to ____ by the committee.
rewrite.explanationRu: Пассив после needs to: needs to be formulated.

definitionEn: forward, onward or out into view; mostly used in fixed formal phrases
senseNote: Почти всегда в устойчивых сочетаниях: set forth, put forth, come forth, hold forth, and so forth, back and forth.
situation: Formal writing or speech about presenting ideas publicly, or about someone stepping out to be seen or heard.

examples.text: After the appeal on television, three new witnesses came [[forth]].
The treaty sets [[forth]] clear rules for fishing in shared waters.
My uncle loves to hold [[forth]] on politics at family dinners.

texts: The committee put [[forth]] a bold plan to save the old harbour.
Nobody has come [[forth]] to claim the lost wallet.
Spring brings [[forth]] fresh green leaves on every tree.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Продвигаться вперёд» с проектом — move forward или go ahead. Forth живёт в книжных сочетаниях: put forth, set forth, come forth.

collocationTask.prompt: set ___ the terms of the agreement
collocationTask.explanationRu: Set forth (книжн.) — «излагать»: условия, правила, доводы. Set about — «браться за дело», set apart — «выделять», set upon — «нападать».

nuance.text: In her opening speech, the lawyer set [[forth]] the main arguments for the defence.
nuance.explanationRu: Set forth — книжное «изложить»: доводы, условия, правила. С глаголом set слово forward так не работает; в нейтральной речи говорят set out или put forward.

reverse.text: I'm really looking [[forward]] to seeing you next week.
reverse.explanationRu: «Ждать с нетерпением» — только look forward to. Forth — книжное слово из сочетаний put forth, set forth.

fixIt.text: Bring your laptop, charger, notes and so [[further]].
fixIt.explanationRu: «И так далее» — and so on или более книжное and so forth. And so further — калька с русского.

definitionEn: willing to give information or talk openly about something
senseNote: Здесь — «охотно рассказывающий» (not very forthcoming about...); значение «предстоящий» (the forthcoming elections) проще.
situation: Describing whether a person is willing to answer questions and share details openly.

examples.text: The manager wasn't very [[forthcoming]] about why three senior staff had suddenly left.
When we asked about the missing money, the treasurer was surprisingly [[forthcoming]] and showed us every receipt.
Teenagers are rarely [[forthcoming]] about their social lives, so don't take it personally.

texts: The minister was not [[forthcoming]] with details of the deal.
My landlord is never very [[forthcoming]] about repair dates.
Ask her directly; she's usually quite [[forthcoming]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Общительный человек — outgoing или sociable. Forthcoming — «охотно делящийся сведениями», обычно в ответ на вопросы.

collocationTask.prompt: She wasn't very ___ about her reasons for leaving.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Forthcoming about — «охотно рассказывающий о чём-то». Upcoming — «предстоящий», oncoming — «встречный», outgoing — «общительный»; с about их так не используют.

nuance.text: The new tenant is polite but not very [[forthcoming]] about her past.
nuance.explanationRu: Forthcoming — готов делиться сведениями, отвечать на вопросы. Outgoing — общительный по характеру; с about его не сочетают, и о готовности рассказывать оно не говорит.

reverse.text: He's very [[outgoing]] and loves meeting new people.
reverse.explanationRu: Общительный, любящий компании — outgoing. Forthcoming говорит о готовности рассказывать, а не о характере в целом.

fixIt.text: The company has been less than [[upcoming]] about the risks of the new product.
fixIt.explanationRu: Upcoming — «предстоящий». Неохотно делиться сведениями — be less than forthcoming about something.

reply.context: A friend asks: "So, did your landlord explain why the rent is going up?"
options: Not really. He was very forthcoming, so he refused to tell me anything.
Not really. He wasn't very forthcoming; he just muttered something about costs.
Regrettably, the lessor was insufficiently forthcoming regarding the aforementioned increase.
reply.explanationRu: Not very forthcoming — «не особо рвался объяснять». Very forthcoming значит «охотно всё рассказал», это противоречит отказу говорить. Третий ответ — канцелярит, а не разговор с другом.

definitionEn: to encourage a feeling, skill or idea to develop over time
senseNote: Здесь — «способствовать развитию» (foster creativity); значение «взять ребёнка на воспитание» (foster a child) не тренируем.
situation: A school, company or community creates conditions that help good qualities, habits or relationships grow.

examples.text: Good teachers [[foster]] curiosity by letting students ask questions instead of just memorising facts.
Open-plan offices were supposed to [[foster]] teamwork, but many employees simply wear headphones all day.
The street festival aims to [[foster]] understanding between the city's many different communities.

texts: Shared meals can [[foster]] a strong sense of family.
The government offers tax breaks to [[foster]] innovation in small firms.
Coaches try to [[foster]] a positive attitude after every defeat.

badCollocation.noteRu: Продажи и прибыль не foster, а boost или increase. Foster — про качества, отношения и идеи: foster trust, foster creativity.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Развивать качество — foster. Raise и bring up — растить детей, educate — давать образование; с creativity их не сочетают.

nuance.text: Good libraries [[foster]] curiosity and a love of reading.
nuance.explanationRu: Foster — создавать условия, чтобы качество развивалось: foster curiosity. Educate — учить, просвещать людей; с curiosity или love of reading его не сочетают.

reverse.text: The charity [[educates]] the public about healthy eating.
reverse.explanationRu: Просвещать людей о чём-то — educate someone about something. В значении «развивать» foster относится к качествам и отношениям, а не к людям.

fixIt.text: Our aim is to [[raise]] a culture of openness in which everyone feels free to speak.
fixIt.explanationRu: Культуру, атмосферу, доверие не raise, а foster — «создавать условия для развития». Raise — растить детей или поднимать.

reply.context: At a staff meeting, your manager asks: "How can we get different departments to work together more?"
options: We could foster the printer in the corridor so everyone shares it.
We could run joint projects. That would foster cooperation without forcing it.
Dunno, just foster some good vibes or whatever.
reply.explanationRu: Foster cooperation — «способствовать сотрудничеству». Принтер нельзя foster: глагол говорит о развитии качеств и отношений. Третий ответ слишком небрежен для рабочей встречи.

definitionEn: weak and uncertain, and therefore easily damaged or destroyed
senseNote: Здесь — о мире, экономике, отношениях: «хрупкий, шаткий»; буквальное значение (fragile glass) проще.
situation: Describing a peace deal, economy or relationship that could easily break down or collapse.

examples.text: The ceasefire is still [[fragile]], and both sides accuse each other of breaking it.
After two years of recession, the recovery remains [[fragile]] and could easily stall.
Their friendship was still [[fragile]] after the argument, so she chose her words carefully.

texts: The two parties formed a [[fragile]] coalition after the election.
Tourism is a [[fragile]] industry that depends on good news.
Her confidence is still [[fragile]] after months out of work.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Уязвимый к чему-то» — vulnerable to. Fragile не требует предлога: a fragile economy.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Перемирие, которое легко сорвать, — a fragile ceasefire. Breakable — о бьющихся предметах, fragmentary — «отрывочный», thin — «тонкий».

nuance.text: Relations between the two neighbours remain [[fragile]] after years of conflict.
nuance.explanationRu: Fragile — о том, что легко разрушить: мир, отношения, восстановление экономики. Flimsy — «хлипкий»: тонкая ткань, шаткая конструкция, неубедительная отговорка.

reverse.text: He gave a [[flimsy]] excuse for missing the meeting.
reverse.explanationRu: Неубедительная отговорка — a flimsy excuse. Fragile описывает то, что может разрушиться, а не слабый довод.

fixIt.text: Experts warn that the peace between the two countries is still very [[breakable]].
fixIt.explanationRu: Breakable говорят о посуде и других предметах. Хрупкий мир, хрупкая экономика — fragile.

wordFormation.text: The crisis exposed the [[fragility]] of the country's banking system.

reply.context: Your colleague asks: "Should we launch the new product now or wait until spring?"
options: I'd wait. Consumer confidence is still pretty fragile after the price rises.
Let's launch now. Our confidence is so fragile that nothing can shake it.
One would posit that the market's fragile disposition necessitates postponement.
reply.explanationRu: Fragile — «шаткий, легко разрушимый». Во втором ответе fragile противоречит словам «ничто не поколеблет». Третий звучит как научная статья, а не рабочий разговор.

definitionEn: permission to run a business using a big company's name and products
senseNote: Здесь — деловое значение «франшиза»; «право голоса» (формальное) и «серия фильмов» (a film franchise) — другие значения.
situation: Someone pays a large company to open a shop or café using its brand name and system.

examples.text: She bought a coffee-shop [[franchise]] instead of starting a business from scratch.
Each [[franchise]] pays the parent company a share of its monthly profits.
The pizza chain now has over 300 [[franchises]] across the country, mostly run by local families.

texts: Opening a [[franchise]] usually costs less than launching your own brand.
The gym [[franchise]] in our town closed after two years.
He signed a ten-year [[franchise]] agreement with a burger chain.

badCollocation.noteRu: Страховая «франшиза» по-английски — excess (брит.) или deductible (амер.). Franchise — право работать под чужим брендом.

collocationTask.prompt: open a ___ of a well-known coffee chain
collocationTask.explanationRu: Работать под брендом сети — open a franchise. Filial значит «сыновний, дочерний», а не «филиал»; department и division — отделы внутри компании.

nuance.text: Instead of opening its own shops, the company sells [[franchises]] to local owners.
nuance.explanationRu: Franchise — право вести бизнес под чужим брендом; точка принадлежит местному владельцу. Branch — филиал, которым владеет сама компания, поэтому продавать branches владельцам нельзя.

reverse.text: The bank is closing its [[branch]] in our village next month.
reverse.explanationRu: Отделение банка, которым владеет сам банк, — branch. Franchise — бизнес, который владелец купил право вести под брендом.

fixIt.text: My uncle bought a [[filial]] of a popular pizza chain and now runs it with his sons.
fixIt.explanationRu: Filial — «сыновний», а не «филиал». Купить право работать под брендом сети — buy a franchise.

wordFormation.text: [[Franchising]] lets a brand grow quickly without opening its own shops.

reply.context: A friend says: "I'd love to open a café, but I've never run a business."
options: Have you considered a franchise? It's when you insure your café against fire.
Might I propose the acquisition of a franchise, thereby mitigating operational risk?
Have you considered a franchise? You'd get a known brand, a tested menu and training.
reply.explanationRu: Franchise — право работать под известным брендом, с его меню и поддержкой. Страховка тут ни при чём. Второй ответ звучит как бизнес-презентация, а не совет другу.

definitionEn: used to show that you are giving your honest opinion, even if it is unwelcome
senseNote: Здесь — вводное «честно говоря» (Frankly, ...); значение «откровенно» (speak frankly) проще.
situation: Before giving an honest opinion or admitting something that the other person may not want to hear.

examples.text: [[Frankly]], your essay is too long, and the main argument gets lost halfway through.
I'm not sure the new app is worth the money; [[frankly]], I preferred the old one.
Thanks for asking my opinion, but [[frankly]], I think the plan is doomed.

texts: Well, [[frankly]], I expected more from such an expensive hotel.
The service was slow and, [[frankly]], a little rude.
She's talented, but [[frankly]], she isn't ready to lead a team.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Честно говоря» — frankly или frankly speaking, но не frankly saying: это калька с русского.

collocationTask.prompt: Quite ___, I don't think he's the right person for the job.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Quite frankly — «если уж честно», перед неприятной правдой. Openly, directly и sincerely вводными словами в начале фразы не бывают.

nuance.text: [[Frankly]], I think we're paying far too much for this office.
nuance.explanationRu: Frankly в начале фразы — «честно говоря», перед неприятной правдой. Sincerely — «искренне» (sincerely hope, sincerely thank); вводным словом его не ставят.

reverse.text: We [[sincerely]] apologise for the delay to your order.
reverse.explanationRu: Искренние извинения — sincerely apologise. Frankly предупреждает о прямоте, а не выражает искренние чувства.

fixIt.text: [[Openly]] speaking, I think the new logo looks cheap and old-fashioned.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Откровенно говоря» — frankly (speaking), а не openly speaking. Openly — «открыто, не скрываясь».

wordFormation.text: I really appreciated the [[frankness]] of her feedback on my presentation.

reply.context: A colleague asks you: "Be honest. Should I apply for the manager's job?"
options: Frankly, I think you're ready. You already do half of that job anyway.
Frankly, I'd rather keep my honest opinion a secret from you.
Frankly, the applicant's suitability shall be evaluated in accordance with procedure.
reply.explanationRu: Frankly вводит честное мнение. Во втором ответе слово противоречит смыслу: человек как раз не хочет говорить честно. Третий звучит как казённый документ.

definitionEn: annoyed and impatient because you cannot do or achieve what you want
senseNote: Основное значение — досада, когда что-то не получается; именно его Oxford относит к C1. Важно не путать с disappointed и upset.
situation: You keep trying to do something, but problems or other people stop you, and you feel annoyed.

examples.text: After an hour on hold with the bank, I was so [[frustrated]] that I hung up.
Many nurses are [[frustrated]] that endless paperwork keeps them away from their patients.
The striker looked [[frustrated]] as yet another shot hit the post.

texts: Voters are [[frustrated]] with the slow pace of change.
I get [[frustrated]] when my laptop freezes during calls.
When you're learning a language, feeling [[frustrated]] is completely normal.

badCollocation.noteRu: Frustrated — досада от препятствий. О горе и печали говорят upset, sad или heartbroken.

collocationTask.prompt: She grew increasingly ___ with the lack of progress.
collocationTask.explanationRu: О чувствах человека — прилагательное на -ed: frustrated with something. Frustrating, disappointing и upsetting описывают то, что вызывает эти чувства.

nuance.text: I've been trying to fix this printer all morning, and I'm getting really [[frustrated]].
nuance.explanationRu: Frustrated — раздражение, когда что-то раз за разом не получается. Disappointed — разочарование, когда ожидания не оправдались; к борьбе с принтером оно не подходит.

reverse.text: I was [[disappointed]] with the film; the book was much better.
reverse.explanationRu: Фильм не оправдал ожиданий — disappointed. Frustrated означает досаду от препятствий, а не разочарование.

fixIt.text: I'm so [[frustrating]] with this website; it keeps logging me out!
fixIt.explanationRu: О своих чувствах — frustrated (-ed). Frustrating описывает то, что раздражает: this website is frustrating.

wordFormation.text: Tenants are increasingly [[frustrated]] by the landlord's failure to fix the heating.

reply.context: A colleague messages you: "How's the new accounting software going?"
options: Great! I'm so frustrated with how smoothly everything works.
Not great, to be honest. I'm frustrated because it crashes every time I save.
Current user status: frustrated. Awaiting technical intervention.
reply.explanationRu: Frustrated — досада, когда что-то мешает. Радоваться гладкой работе этим словом нельзя. Третий ответ звучит как сообщение робота, а не коллеги.

rewrite.original: The long delays really annoyed the passengers.
rewrite.frame: The passengers were really ____ the long delays.
